history.summary: This is a sub-shrine near the main Shani temple at Shani Shingnapur (reported ~400 m from the Shani Shingnapur bus stand), dedicated to Lord Dattatreya, worshipped as the combined form of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. It is one of the subsidiary shrines within the Shani Shingnapur temple complex area, listed alongside the Lakshmi Temple, the Udasi Baba samadhi and the Brahmin Pushkarni stepwell. UNVERIFIED: no independent sources found for its founding date, builder, trusteeship or history, and no verifiable photograph of this specific shrine was found after genuine searching, so media is empty. Coordinates are those of the main Shani temple complex (approximate).

name: Dattatray Shrine, Shani Shingnapur Complex
town_description: Shani Shingnapur (also spelled Shinganapur) is a village in Nevasa taluka of Ahmednagar district, Maharashtra, about 35 km from Ahmednagar. It is world-famous for its roofless open-air shrine of Lord Shani and for its tradition of houses without doors or locks, trusting in the deity's protection. The temple complex includes subsidiary shrines to Datta, Lakshmi, Ganesh, Shiva and Vishnu.

travel.road: The shrine stands near the Shani temple, ~400 m from the Shani Shingnapur bus stand (verify).
